comment: The agent-key gate for this repository. Read tools/agent-gate.mjs's header before
trusting anything here: this file is the RECEIPT, not the lock. It stops a copied
tree, a borrowed laptop and a casual collaborator, and it makes a deliberate edit
leave a trail. It cannot stop someone who has the bytes — they delete this file.
The real lock is a GitHub ruleset on main: run `agent-gate.mjs lock-status`.
HASHES ONLY. Never put a key in this file: it is committed, and the repo's own
pre-commit guard scans staged content for exactly that mistake. The key lives at
sha256 = sha256('aegiscode-agent-gate-v1\n' + key)  — see KEY_DOMAIN in tools/agent-gate.mjs
The engine re-implements this in aegiscodex-dev/src/repoguard.js; a shared test
vector in aegiscode-plugin/test/agent-gate.test.mjs holds the two in step.

keys.burnedReason: rotated (disclosed in a chat transcript; rotated from aegiscode-plugin, mirrored here to match)

machinesNote: Machine binding is a speed bump, not identity: the fingerprint is a hash of public facts plus a per-install salt (keys/machine.salt), so it is reproducible on this install and not by guessing. Adding a machine is explicit (bind-machine); moving the key file does not carry the binding. `init` binds the machine that runs it, because the alternative is an operator locked out by their own manifest.
